reasoning: Read the whole packing path on both sides. TagFixWallGranPackExchange (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:368-381) does 'const int i = d_sendlist(mysend); int m = i*size_history; for (int v = 0; v < size_history; v++) d_buf(m++) = ...d_history_one(i,v);' -- the destination offset is derived from the LOCAL ATOM INDEX i, not from the send slot mysend. pack_exchange_kokkos returns 'nsend*size_history' (line 410), and comm_kokkos.cpp:1404 does 'MPI_Send(k_buf_send...data(), nextrasend, MPI_DOUBLE, ...)' i.e. it transmits exactly the first nsend*size_history doubles of the buffer; comm_kokkos.cpp:1371-1372 only guarantees 'nsend*fix_iextra->maxexchange' doubles of capacity. So the packed values land at arbitrary offsets up to nlocal*size_history (outside both the transmitted window and, in general, the allocated buffer). Both sibling implementations index by the send slot: fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:383-385 'int m = nsend + offset; d_buf(mysend) = d_ubuf(m).d;' and fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:186-187 'int m = nsend + offset; d_buf[mysend] = m;'. Nothing compensates elsewhere -- the unpack side (line 422) also assumes slot-major layout ('int m = i*size_history'), which is only consistent with a slot-indexed pack.
fix: In operator()(TagFixWallGranPackExchange,...) replace 'int m = i*size_history;' with 'int m = mysend*size_history;'. (The atom index i must still be used for the d_history_one reads and for the d_copylist compaction.)

reasoning: TagFixWallGranUnpackExchange (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:418-426) reads 'int index = d_indices(i); if (index > -1) { int m = i*size_history; for (...) d_history_one(i,v) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(d_buf(m++)); }'. The mapped destination 'index' is computed and then used only as a guard; the store target is the receive slot i. Every sibling that implements this hook stores at the mapped index: fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:260-262 'd_xoriginal(index,0) = ...', fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:467-471 'd_npartner(index) = n; d_partner(index,p) = ...'. d_indices is filled by AtomVecKokkos::unpack_exchange_kokkos (comm_kokkos.cpp:1358-1360) and holds the local atom index each received atom was placed at, which is only accidentally equal to i. Nothing later repairs this: the history is written by no other code path on the device side. Note the buffer offset 'i*size_history' is itself fine for a fixed-size record (the two receive segments are contiguous for fixed record size), so this line needs only the destination index changed.
fix: Change the store to 'd_history_one(index,v) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(d_buf(m++));' (keep 'int m = i*size_history;').

reasoning: The pairstyle half is real. FixWallGranKokkos derives from FixWallGranOld (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.h:38), whose constructor accepts 'granular' (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:83 'else if (strcmp(arg[3],"granular") == 0) pairstyle = GRANULAR;') and whose class enum is 'HOOKE, HOOKE_HISTORY, HERTZ_HISTORY, GRANULAR' (fix_wall_gran_old.h:29). post_force (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:107-119) is 'if (pairstyle == HOOKE) error->all(...); else if (pairstyle == HOOKE_HISTORY) {...} else if (pairstyle == HERTZ_HISTORY) error->all(...);' with no trailing else, so pairstyle == GRANULAR launches no kernel and raises no error; the fix silently applies zero wall force. Since the style is registered as wall/gran/kk (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.h:16), 'fix ... wall/gran granular ...' under -sf kk hits exactly this path. Note the class-scope enumerators win over the file-local 'enum{HOOKE,HOOKE_HISTORY,HERTZ_HISTORY,BONDED_HISTORY};' at line 24 (member lookup precedes namespace lookup) and both have the same numeric values, so the shadowing enum is only a readability problem, not the cause. ADJUSTMENT: the REGION half is not a KOKKOS port defect -- FixWallGranOld::post_force (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:645-677) has no REGION branch either (it would leave dx=dy=dz=0, rsq=0 and divide by r=0), so wallstyle 'region' is broken in the base class this port copies; the KOKKOS behaviour (no kernel) is different but the CPU reference is not correct either.
fix: Add a final 'else error->all(FLERR, "Fix wall/gran/kk does not yet support the granular interaction style");' to the pairstyle chain in FixWallGranKokkos::post_force, and an 'else error->all(FLERR, ...)' (or a check in init()) for wallstyle values other than XPLANE/YPLANE/ZPLANE/ZCYLINDER. Better still, reject the unsupported pairstyle/wallstyle in FixWallGranKokkos::init() so the error appears at setup rather than on every timestep. Also rename the file-local enumerator BONDED_HISTORY to GRANULAR (or delete the shadowing enum) so it matches fix_wall_gran_old.h.

reasoning: Read both kernels side by side. CPU FixWallGranOld::hooke_history (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:898-900): 'damp = meff*gamman*vnnr*rsqinv; ccel = kn*(radius-r)*rinv - damp; if (limit_damping && (ccel < 0.0)) ccel = 0.0;'. The KOKKOS kernel (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:226-227) has only 'KK_FLOAT damp = meff*gamman_kk*vnnr*rsqinv; KK_FLOAT ccel = kn_kk*(radius-r)*rinv - damp;' and goes straight to the relative-velocity block; the rest of the kernel is a line-for-line copy of hooke_history, so the clamp is the single omission. limit_damping is a genuine keyword parsed for the non-granular pairstyles (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:124-127, iarg==10) and is an int member of the base class (fix_wall_gran_old.h:72) already carried into the functor by the by-value *this copy, so the fix is a one-liner. No compensating clamp exists anywhere else in the KOKKOS file, and ccel also feeds the Coulomb limit 'fn = xmu*fabs(ccel*r)' at line 265, so the tangential force is affected too.
fix: After 'KK_FLOAT ccel = kn_kk*(radius-r)*rinv - damp;' in operator()(TagFixWallGranHookeHistory<WallStyle>,...) add 'if (limit_damping && (ccel < static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.0))) ccel = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.0);'.

reasoning: Traced the whole allocation path. FixWallGranOld's constructor calls the qualified 'FixWallGranOld::grow_arrays(atom->nmax)' (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:450) which allocates BOTH history_one and, when peratom_flag, array_atom (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:1567-1573). The Kokkos constructor then destroys history_one and calls the virtual grow_arrays again (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:44); every later growth goes through Atom::grow -> fix->grow_arrays(nmax) i.e. the Kokkos override (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:303-311), which grows only k_history_one and only 'if (use_history)'. array_atom therefore stays frozen at the initial atom->nmax. The base pack_exchange/copy_arrays that the Kokkos class delegates to still touch it: fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:1584-1587 'array_atom[j][m] = array_atom[i][m];' and :1616-1619 'buf[n++] = array_atom[i][m];'. 'contacts' is a real keyword accepted by the shared constructor (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:410-413, peratom_flag=1, size_peratom_cols=8), so this is reachable with wall/gran/kk. Separately the constructor sets 'maxexchange = size_history;' (line 35) while FixWallGranOld::pack_exchange writes size_history+size_peratom_cols doubles, which undersizes both Comm::maxexchange_fix on the host path and the 'nsend*fix_iextra->maxexchange' grow in comm_kokkos.cpp:1371. And the device kernel never writes array_atom nor calls clear_stored_contacts(), which the CPU post_force does (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:637-639, 713-724), so the per-atom contact output is always zero.
fix: Simplest correct fix: reject the 'contacts' keyword (peratom_flag) in FixWallGranKokkos::init() with an explicit error, as is already done for fix_rigid. If it is to be supported: call FixWallGranOld::grow_arrays()/copy_arrays()/set_arrays() unconditionally for the array_atom part from the Kokkos overrides (they must run even when use_history is 0), set 'maxexchange = size_history + (peratom_flag ? size_peratom_cols : 0);' in the constructor, and have the kernel fill array_atom (plus a clear_stored_contacts equivalent).
